Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is the official handoff from sales to CS — so I'll be quick. Welcome clearshore team — excited to get started. Sofia and Maya from my side with me.
[00:15] Daniel: Hey thanks Ethan, we appreciate it. Quick note, we've been evaluating a couple of approaches but committed to start with Redwood for the pilot. Main goals are: sub-300ms median tail for short messages and predictable monthly spend.
[00:30] Sofia: Great, that aligns w our templates. Quick question on traffic profile — what percent of requests are batched vs single-shot today?
[00:45] Priya: Right now for internal tooling it's mostly single-shot, about 85% are < 50 tokens. We do have a few long-run prompts for summarization, that's the 15%.
[01:00] Sofia: OK good, that helps with kernel selection and batching config. For the pilot we usually suggest starting on hosted and then move to Dedicated if you need strict latency SLOs and isolation — but we can scope a small dedicated pool if that's a blocker for compliance.
[01:20] Marcus: Compliance is a factor, we can't have logs leave region for certain PII processes. Will need details on data residency and purge policies.
[01:35] Maya: Understood — we have region pinning and log retention controls. We'll share the security pack with SOC2, ISO artifacts and the specifics on audit log retention. Sara, maybe you can tell us any immediate constraints?
[01:50] Sara: We have two constraints: 1) logs must be retained for 1 year and stored in our account, not Redwood-managed S3, 2) any key material must be under our KMS or HSM — we prefer HSM for production.
[02:10] Ethan: Noted. For Private deployment we support customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM in the on-prem package; for hosted there are KMS integrations but we need to check HSM options. We'll follow up with the security doc.
[02:30] Daniel: Another question: we want to test the KV cache and prefix caching, our RAG workflows rely on a consistent cache hit rate. Do you expose cache metrics?
[02:45] Sofia: Yes, Console exposes token-level cache hit/miss, per-route breakdowns and per-model metrics. We'll add the sample dashboards to the runbook.
[03:00] Priya: Awesome. On networking, is VPC peering required or do you support private egress via customer NAT? We're air-gapped for some lanes.
[03:15] Sofia: We support both. For Dedicated and Private, VPC peering or PrivateLink is commonly used. For hosted, we can accept requests over a controlled egress with IP allowlist and mutual TLS — depends on the security posture.
[03:35] Marcus: The timeline — we want pilot in two weeks, production in 8 weeks. Is that realistic?
[03:45] Maya: Two weeks for a pilot is realistic as long as we get your VPC details and SSO/SAML info this week. The 8-week production ramp is contingent on SLA decisions and whether you need Dedicated hardware.
[04:00] Ethan: Quick aside: pricing worksheets will show committed capacity discounts; if you lock a small pool for the pilot, we can reserve a few GPUs for predictable throughput.
[04:15] Daniel: Let's talk about success criteria — for pilot we care about error rate < 1%, mean latency < 200ms for single-shot < 50 tokens, 99th percentile < 400ms, and cost per 1k requests within the projected budget.
[04:35] Sofia: We'll run baseline benchmarks with your sample prompts and compare model variants — quantized options too. For shorter prompts, quantization shouldn't materially impact quality but reduces cost.
[04:55] Priya: Any concerns about model weights and IP? We have legal asking about model provenance and derivative data.
[05:10] Ethan: We'll provide the model catalog and licensing notes. For proprietary data you can always choose private deployment where model artifacts remain on your infra.
[05:25] Sara: Can we get audit logs pushed to our SIEM?
[05:35] Maya: Yes, we support delivering audit logs to your S3 or Splunk via connectors, and we can have them streamed into your SIEM. We'll include sample config in the security pack.
[05:50] Daniel: Cool. For the smoke test, what are the steps?
[06:00] Sofia: The smoke test runbook we'll post includes: 1) run a 1k request burst at your expected concurrency, 2) capture tail latency and error rates, 3) validate cache hit metrics, 4) verify SSO access and RBAC with a test user, and 5) validate log delivery. It should take a half day to run.
[06:30] Priya: For the 1k burst, do you have a load harness or should we use our own?
[06:40] Sofia: We can provide a small harness — it's a wrapper that hits the endpoints with configurable concurrency and sends results to a CSV. We'll share the repo link.
[06:55] Marcus: On the subject of rollout policies — can Redwood do canary routing and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if error rate spikes?
[07:10] Sofia: Yes, Console supports rollout policies, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to pinned model variants. You can set policies by error thresholds or latency.
[07:25] Daniel: There was an internal discussion about whether to use streaming vs non-streaming for the UI snippets; streaming might reduce perceived latency. Does SDK support streaming in hosted?
[07:40] Sofia: Streaming is supported in hosted API and Dedicated runtimes. For the web UI, streaming cuts perceived latency but requires the client to handle chunked responses. We'll share front-end SDK examples.
[07:55] Ethan: Let's get into the concrete dates for deliverables — Maya will run the onboarding cadence and set weekly syncs. Maya, can you book the weekly check-ins starting next Thursday?
[08:08] Maya: Yep, I'll send invites for weekly 30-minute check-ins starting 2026-03-25 and include an initial agenda.
[08:16] Sara: One more security note — we need to confirm whether debug logs may contain PII. We need redaction options.
[08:30] Sofia: We have redaction tooling; you can specify what fields to mask and we can filter logs before they land in your account. We'll document that.
[08:45] Daniel: Great. Pricing question from legal: if we go Dedicated, what's the SLA for latency?
[08:55] Ethan: We publish target latency ranges per model family for Dedicated, plus uptime SLAs. We'll send the SLA doc. If you need an enterprise SLA with uptime credits, that's part of the Dedicated contract.
[09:10] Priya: For initial keys/access — how do we onboard engineers? Do you have temporary tokens or do we set up SSO right away?
[09:20] Maya: We provide short-lived API keys for initial smoke tests but prefer SSO/SAML for ongoing access and RBAC. We'll create service accounts for your CI/CD with scoped permissions.
[09:35] Marcus: Any gotchas you've seen in deployments like ours (logistics, event-driven, high request volume at end-of-day)?
[09:45] Sofia: Common gotchas: 1) underestimating burst concurrency — provisioning burst capacity helps; 2) not using prefix caching for repeated prompts; 3) missing firewall rules for KV cache egress. We'll add a preflight checklist.
[10:05] Daniel: Alright let's talk about who owns what — do we have the handoff roster spelled out?
[10:12] Maya: Yes — CS will own onboarding and weekly cadence, SE (Sofia) will own the benchmark runs and smoke test, AE (Ethan) remains the contract owner for pricing, and customer (Daniel/Priya) will provide infra details and sample datasets.
[10:25] Ethan: We'll also cc legal/security to the thread once Sara sends the checklist.
[10:30] Priya: I'll add the VPC ranges and firewall egress by Monday.
[10:36] Sara: And I'll share the compliance doc with HSM preferences.
[10:40] Sofia: For the pilot benchmarking, are you okay with us using model variants (e.g., int8 quant) to compare cost/latency/quality tradeoffs?
[10:50] Daniel: Yes, but we want a blind eval set so our product folks can't bias the selection.
[10:58] Sofia: Perfect, we'll coordinate a blind eval and provide the metrics.
[11:05] Marcus: Any dependencies on our side besides VPC and SSO?
[11:12] Maya: Sample prompts, a small test corpus for quality checks, and an owner for approval of rollout criteria.
[11:18] Daniel: I'll assign an internal owner for approvals.
[11:22] Ethan: Great. Last item: do we want a short technical deep-dive for your infra folks next week? It can cover kernel selection, KV cache, and quantization tradeoffs.
[11:33] Priya: Yes please — schedule a 60-minute SE deep-dive with our infra team.
[11:38] Sofia: We'll prepare slides and a short benchmark demo.
[11:44] Maya: I'll create a shared drive with all the onboarding artifacts: runbook, security pack, pricing, and the harness link. Expect the folder invite today.
[11:52] Daniel: Sounds good. Anything else?
[11:55] Marcus: No, thanks all. Looking forward to the pilot.
[12:00] Ethan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and the scheduling items. End call.
